card.name: The word that before a clause
card.fires_on: The word "that" (sometimes "this", "if" or a question mark) right after a verb or noun, where a clause or explanation is about to follow. It appears in ordinary web prose.

modes.label: that after do/who/what
modes.description: "that" as object or relative word after "do", "it was", or "is it", leading into a clause.
modes.example: there is only one person on earth who can do<< that>>, and that is Ganapati.

modes.label: that after a noun
modes.description: "that" introducing a relative clause after a noun such as owl or sports.
modes.example: start drawing this owl<< that>> I have drawn for you all

modes.label: Other clause openers
modes.description: A question mark or "if" that ends a phrase and leads into the next clause.
modes.example: Is it killing you<<?>> Well some scientists are beginning to think that

card.plain: It fires on the small word "that" when it links a statement to the clause that follows.
evidence: who it was<< that>> passed it the night before last
not everyone wants to do<< that>>, especially not every day
it could cost a doctor his job<< if>> he speaks the truth
